/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]

Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: DERIVE_FROM_REPO
Q2: REFRAME

RATIONALE:
Q1: Option A asks the respondent to paste step timings from `GET actions/runs/40626853481/jobs`. I don't have them: the GITHUB FACTS block only shows run 40626853481 as `completed/success`, and the sandbox has no GitHub token. Picking A without the data would loop this clarification, which the data-provision guard rules out. Option B guesses from body size, and that already failed under #7387, #7406, #7576, #7677 and #8208. The repo has a better way: under #7690 the step bodies of this same job were timed in the implement sandbox (ci.yml lines 2383–2391 and 2483–2491). Per-job totals come from the recorded budget-watch history in ci.yml comments. Neither needs data from outside the repo.

Q2: The ci.yml comments show that no job has known headroom. Moved steps keep pushing the overrun around:
- `orchestrate-poll` group 3 hit 15m08s (#8072).
- Group 4 hit 15m13s (#8150, lines 2531–2542), even though it only carries the unblock-judge step.
- Group 0 hit 17m01s (#8118) and group 1 hit 16m09s (#8091).
- Group 2 has taken extra steps since its last estimate (#7690, #7798).
- Every `tests-*` job has recorded about 15 minutes or more.
- `static-checks` has only a 15-minute timeout.

When moving failed, the repo twice split a slow step into parallel shards in place instead: the heal step (#7387, lines 933–945) and the unblock step (#8150). That is the safest way to meet the goal. Most of the time this job gained came with the #8208 move-in (lines 1226–1239), so moving those steps back would just recreate #8208.

EXECUTION PLAN:
Q1:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `tests-heal-plan-and-validation` (lines 910–1433), every step body after "Install Python CI dependencies"
    - Earlier timing method and its limits: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 2383–2391 (#7690: relative weights only; PyYAML was missing, so modules that need yaml failed, and the sharded heal step stopped early)
    - Recorded totals and moves per job: ci.yml comments at lines 933–945 (#7387), 1110–1115 (#7406), 1161–1167 (#7576), 1180–1185 (#7677), 1226–1230 (#8208), 2450–2460 (#7798), 2483–2542 (#7690/#8072/#8091/#8118/#8150)
  steps:
    - Time each step body of `tests-heal-plan-and-validation` in the implement sandbox, one at a time, with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. Record wall seconds per step.
    - For pytest-based steps, add `--durations=0` so per-module cost is known. For a step that runs several scripts with `python3 tests/<f>.py`, time each script separately.
    - If a module cannot be timed because of a sandbox limit (missing PyYAML, no network, no Docker), mark it "not measurable". Do not guess its cost. Keep the rest of the step's timings.
    - Treat the numbers as relative weights only, as #7690 did. Name the 2–3 heaviest steps or modules as the candidates. Expected candidates, still to be confirmed by timing: "Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 1)", "Release CI gate tests (stubbed gh; both release workflows)", "Clarify loop guard unit tests", and the unsharded tail of "Workflow failure heal contract and driver tests" (the `test_workflow_failure_heal_*` follow-on and `test_provider_outage.py` commands at lines 999–1001).
    - Write the measured weights, the "not measurable" list, and the run reference (run 40626853481, this issue) into a ci.yml comment above each changed step, in the same style as lines 2383–2391.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "see the run's step timings" (CI step timings for run 40626853481)
  equivalence_argument: The issue wants the slowest steps picked from evidence rather than guessed. Timing each step in the sandbox does that, and the repo already used this method for this exact job (#7690). CI step timings can't be read from the planner or implementer sandbox.
  reversibility: Only a ci.yml comment and the choice of steps depend on this. If a person later supplies the real CI step timings, the next budget-watch round can choose again from those, using the same steps.

Q2:
  strategy: reframe
  inputs:
    - The sharding pattern to copy: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 930–998 (heal step: collect with `pytest --collect-only`, deduplicate test functions, split with `NR % total == n` into 4 background pytest processes, wait for every shard, a missing `.rc` counts as failed, failing shard tails are printed again) and lines 2543–2560+ (unblock step, the same pattern over several modules)
    - The candidate list measured in Q1
    - `tests/test_ci_job_split_contract.py` (aggregate `needs`, budgets, no step in two jobs) and `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` (every test file still named in a workflow)
  steps:
    - For each of the 1–2 heaviest pytest-based candidates from Q1 (for example "Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 1)"), shard the step in place across 4 local pytest processes, using the pattern from lines 930–998 exactly. Keep the step's `name:`, its job, its module list and `set -euo pipefail`. Collection errors print the raw collect log and fail. Each collected test function runs exactly once. Any shard without exit code 0 fails the step.
    - Do not shard a step whose tests run as `python3 tests/<f>.py` with a `__main__` runner (for example "Release CI gate tests", "Clarify loop guard unit tests"). Leave those bodies byte-identical.
    - If sharding the measured candidates in place cannot plausibly bring the job under 15 minutes (pytest-based candidates add up to less than about a third of the measured step time), use Q2 option A as the fallback. Move the heaviest script-style step(s) unchanged, with name and body intact, splitting them across two of the four `tests-*` jobs. Never move a step into `static-checks` or any `orchestrate-poll` group. Never move "Release CI gate tests" or "Mark-stable release-tag refspec contract test" back into `tests-release-and-log-analysis` (#8208). Prefer `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`, which had three steps moved out in #7798 and nothing recorded moved in since. Add a "Moved from …" comment that cites this issue and the measured weights.
    - Do not change any `timeout-minutes`, job name or step name, and do not add jobs. The `lint` aggregate's `needs` list stays the same.
    - Above each sharded step, add a "Sharded in place, not moved (this issue)" comment citing #7387 and #8150 as precedent and run 40626853481's 15m06s.
    - Run `tests/test_ci_job_split_contract.py`, `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` and actionlint/yamllint on ci.yml. Run each sharded step's commands locally where the sandbox allows.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "Move its slowest steps … into the CI job with the most headroom"
  equivalence_argument: The issue's real requirement is that this job finishes well under its 20-minute timeout, with no timeout raised and no new required job names. Sharding the slowest steps in place shortens this job and adds no time to any other job. A move would land on jobs that the recorded history shows are already at about 15 minutes (#8072, #8091, #8118, #8150 and the `tests-*` issues), and each earlier move just reopened budget-watch somewhere else. Job and step names, test sets and timeouts stay the same. The issue's literal remedy, moving to two existing `tests-*` jobs (Q2 option A), is still the fallback.
  reversibility: Each sharded step can go back to its original single-command body with no other change, and a moved step can be moved back. Names, `needs` and timeouts are untouched, so required checks and branch protection are not affected either way.
